title: CRLR/440/2022 of GOVIND SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 440 of 2022
Govind Singh ...... Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and another ..... Respondents
Present:-
Mr. B.S. Bhandari & Mr. Narendra Singh Bisht, Advocates for the
revisionists.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. assisted by Ms. Sonika Khulbe, Brief Holder for
the State.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The revisionist has been convicted under
Section 323 IPC and sentenced for 6 months simple
imprisonment with a fine of Rs. 500/- in Criminal Case
No. 384 of 2015, State of Uttarakhand Vs. Govind Singh,
on 22.05.2017, by the court of Judicial Magistrate,
Nainital. His conviction was upheld in Criminal Appeal
No.65 of 2017, Govind Singh Vs. State of Uttarakhand,
by the court of Second Additional Sessions Judge,
Nainital. Both these orders are impugned in this
revision.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.

2
3. According to the prosecution case, on
25.09.2014, there was a meeting in the village at 5:00
P.M. Thereafter, while the injured PW1 Ramesh Chand
was returning home, at about 5:45 P.M., he was
assaulted by the revisionist. It is this case, in which after
investigation, chargesheet under Sections 323, 504 &
506 was filed against the revisionist, but was convicted
and sentenced under Section 323 IPC and has been
acquitted under Section 504 & 506 IPC. In appeal, in
fact, only the question of sentence was raised.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that the revisionist has been sentenced under
Section 323 IPC; it is a case of simple Marpeet in a
village area; there has been no enmity between the
parties as such; the revisionist is in custody for the last
5 days. Therefore, instead of sentence, his fine may be
enhanced.
5. It is told that the revisionist is a small
farmer.
6. On behalf of the State, it is fairly conceded
that the fine may be increased.
7. Having considered the entirety of facts, this
Court is of the view that while upholding the conviction,

3
the sentence may be modified to the extent that the
revisionist shall pay a fine of Rs. 5,000/- under Section
323 IPC.
8. The revisionist is sentenced under Section
323 IPC with a fine of Rs. 5,000/-. In default of payment
of fine, the revisionist shall undergo simple
imprisonment for a period of one month.
9. The impugned judgment and orders are
modified to the extent, as above.
10. The revision is disposed of accordingly.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 05.08.2022
